title: FinOps for LLMs — Unit Economics and Multi-Tenant Attribution

questions.question: Which three attribution dimensions does the lesson recommend instrumenting on day one?
options: Region, GPU type, and kernel version
Prompt length, batch size, and cache TTL
user_id, task_id plus route, and tenant_id
questions.explanation: The lesson's unit-economics view tags per user, per task/route, and per tenant so spend can be tied to people, product surfaces, and contracts.

questions.question: Which four token layers does the lesson say a single billing bucket can hide?
questions.explanation: The four layers are prompt, tool, memory, and response; separating them exposes prompt bloat and tool or memory amplification.

questions.question: What daily spend cap does TenantPolicy give tenant_A_normal?
questions.explanation: tenant_A_normal has contracted_daily_usd=100 and spend_cap_multiplier=2.0, so the cap check compares spend with $200.

questions.question: When can the FinOps simulator activate the kill switch?
options: On the first request of every day
After at least five history points when spend z-score exceeds 4
Whenever a tenant uses more than 40 requests per minute
Only when daily spend is exactly zero
questions.explanation: simulate_day requires len(daily_history) >= 5, computes z, and pauses when z > policy.kill_z_score, which defaults to 4.0.

questions.question: Which tenant is configured with traffic_mult=25.0 in TENANTS?
questions.explanation: tenant_C_abusive is the tuple with a $20 contract, 40 requests/minute, and traffic multiplier 25.0.

questions.question: Which product metric does the lesson prefer over a raw $/M-token number?
options: Cost per resolved query or generated artifact
questions.explanation: A unit such as cost per resolved support query ties token spend to product value; $/M tokens alone cannot show whether a task succeeded.
